subject: Urgent: Hosted API p95/p99 spike impacting ACME production - runtime memory fragmentation suspected
messages:
From: Katie Long <katie.long@acme.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 16:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: sudden p95/p99 regressions on hosted - impact to production

Stephanie —

We started seeing a sustained p95/p99 latency increase across our calls to /v1/generate starting ~15:30 UTC today. Errors briefly spiked to 5% with 503s, and overall throughput dropped as we saw retry amplification. This is affecting our user-facing inference feature (about 20% traffic routed to Redwood). I attached a small screenshot from our dashboard showing the p99 climb and the error bursts (acme_latency_20270529.png).

Can you confirm whether this is something on Redwood's side? Our SREs found repeated runtime OOM traces in the logs around the same time. We're on the hosted plan. We need an ETA on mitigation — this is impacting our customers.

-Katie
Katie Long
VP Product Operations, ACME Corp

Attachments: acme_latency_20270529.png (image/png)

-Stephanie

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 16:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: sudden p95/p99 regressions on hosted - impact to production

Stephanie / team — initial findings from runtime side:

- Correlation: p99 spikes line up with repeated GPU memory allocation failures and subsequent small OOMs in the serving nodes that host ACME traffic (see attached runtime_heap_snapshot_20270529.tgz). Kernel traces show slab fragmentation and frequent KV cache eviction thrash between 15:27–15:45 UTC.
- Likely cause: a workload pattern shifted today (longer sequences + a sudden burst of concurrent sessions) causing our allocator to fragment device memory on a subset of hosts. This leads to transient OOMs and request retries that amplify tail latency.

Immediate mitigations applied (15:40 UTC):
1) Temporarily reduced max_batch_size for ACME's route from 16 -> 8 (reduces allocation pressure).
2) Enabled soft-preempt on affected pools to favor smaller inference jobs and reduce long-running kernels.
3) Forced a rolling restart on 4 hosts showing highest fragmentation.

Preliminary result: p99 has dropped ~40% in affected zones but not fully back to baseline. We pushed a diagnostic heap snapshot and logs to the incident ticket. I also attached a short commands file (mitigation_commands.txt) with the exact commands we ran.

Next steps:
- run targeted KV cache warmup and increase the preferred quantized kernel to reduce transient allocations;
- schedule a remediation deploy to improve our allocator heuristics (INF-7213).

I'll keep monitoring; if we continue to see residual tail we should consider routing ACME traffic to a lower-latency pool (dedicated nodes) while we roll a durable fix.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runtime_heap_snapshot_20270529.tgz (logs), mitigation_commands.txt (text)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Katie — thanks for the quick heads up and apologies for the impact. Stephanie and Dylan are triaging; we applied an initial mitigation (reduced batching + rolling restarts) and saw partial improvement.

Proposed immediate customer actions:
- We'll keep these mitigations in place for the next 4 hours while we monitor.
- If your traffic continues to see degradation, we can route your production traffic to an isolated pool (short-lived dedicated capacity) as a temporary measure while we fix the allocator.
- We'll offer a one-time service credit relative to the degraded window (TBD with Sales/Finance).

Can you confirm whether you want us to route to the isolated pool if we still see issues after monitoring, or would you prefer us to continue on-hosted while we implement the allocator patch?

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 18:10:00 +0000
Subject: Exec summary / approval: ACME production impact (p99) and recommended remediation

Team — quick exec note for Priyom: ACME (large enterprise customer, ACME-4892) experienced a p95/p99 regression correlated with GPU memory fragmentation on hosted pools. Impact window began 2027-05-29 15:27 UTC; mitigation reduced p99 but hasn't fully normalized. Customer traffic represents ~20% of their product requests and this is customer-visible.

Recommended immediate actions (need sign-off):
- Offer ACME a one-time credit (we should pre-approve up to $10k gross credit) to expedite resolution and preserve relationship.
- Offer temporary migration of their critical route to an isolated pool (dedicated short-term nodes) while runtime pushes allocator fix (estimated deploy in 72 hours).
- Prioritize INF-7213 (allocator heuristics) for next deploy window and schedule postmortem within 48 hours.

Dylan: please confirm estimated SLA for durable fix timeline.
Priyom: please confirm credit approval and whether to loop Finance/legal for quick approval.

-Stephanie

Appreciate your patience — we understand the impact and are treating this with exec attention.

Best,
